subject: Defining certification criteria and closure checkpoints for Aurelius pilot
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Bloom <emma@aureliushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance tests (Aurelius pilot)

Hi Emma —

Following our call last week, attaching a first-pass mutual action plan and a short list of acceptance tests we typically run for pilots like yours. High level goals here: reduce integration unknowns, agree on measurable pass/fail for the 30-day pilot, and define a clean path to procurement signoff.

Quick summary of what’s in the attachments:
- MAP-draft.xlsx — milestone owner, timing, deliverables for each sprint (integration, model tuning, safety checks, go/no-go)
- eval-test-cases.md — curated smoke + edge-case test vectors we’ll run against the model outputs
- Aurelius_Security_QA.pdf — your security questions filled out where we could; flagged a couple items for your security team to confirm

A few asks to help us finalize the plan:
1) Who on your side will own the integration milestones? (name + email) — we left this blank in the MAP
2) Are the three acceptance tests in eval-test-cases.md representative of your success criteria or do we need to add clinical safety thresholds?
3) Procurement: what lead time do you need for a purchase order or SOW after pilot signoff?

Proposed timeline (high level):
- Week 0–1: integration + environment validation (shared staging)
- Week 2: run smoke tests and initial quality check; collect metrics
- Week 3: remediation loop (model config, prompt tuning)
- Week 4: final evaluation and go/no-go decision

If this looks reasonable I’ll update the MAP with your owners and send a version suitable for DocuSign (if needed).

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: MAP-draft.xlsx, eval-test-cases.md, Aurelius_Security_QA.pdf

From: Emma Bloom <emma@aureliushealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aurelius Procurement <procurement@aureliushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance tests (Aurelius pilot)

Thanks Monica — this is very helpful.

Quick answers:
- Integration owner will be me (Emma Bloom), and I’m looping in Aaron from procurement (procurement@aureliushealth.com) for the commercial steps.
- Clinical safety: we do need a couple of specific thresholds for false-positive rate on triage recommendations and for hallucination-style failures. I added comments to eval-test-cases.md — see the commented sections (edge-case #7 and #12).
- Procurement lead time: typically 2–3 weeks for a standard pilot SOW once we have a final statement of work and price. If we need security review beyond what you provided, that can add 1–2 weeks.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a temporary privacy boundary for PHI in the pilot (redact/store-only-on-customer-side option)? Also can you point me to the SLA we would be evaluating against for the pilot?

Appreciate the clear timeline. One ask from my side: can we add a short acceptance criterion around latency (95th percentile token latency < 150ms) — otherwise product folks will flag perf as a blocker.

— Emma
Emma Bloom
Head of Digital Operations | Aurelius Health
emma@aureliushealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Bloom <emma@aureliushealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance tests (Aurelius pilot)

Hi Emma — thanks for the notes, and great to see Aaron included. I’ll address the items you raised:

1) PHI handling: Redwood can run pilot environments in a customer-managed VPC/private deployment (Redwood Private) where logs and KV cache remain in your VPC. For a hosted pilot we can enable on-the-fly redaction hooks and a policy to avoid persistence of sensitive tokens. I’ll attach an ops note (summarized below).

2) Latency SLA: we can target 95th percentile < 150ms for the API path if the workload fits within the expected token rates and request sizes. If you include long context windows (>1024 tokens) we should update the SLA. For the pilot we recommend a config that keeps context <= 512 tokens for baseline measurements.

3) Clinical safety thresholds: proposed additions to eval-test-cases.md:
- False-positive threshold on triage suggestions: <= 2.5% on the curated safety corpus
- Hallucination rate: measured as ungrounded factual assertions per 1k tokens < 0.8
- Recovery: any failing test must have a mitigation plan and be re-tested within 5 business days

4) Evidence & acceptance: For pass/fail, we suggest a 3-part gating rubric:
- Functional (smoke tests pass)
- Quality (metric thresholds met on test corpus)
- Ops (security checklist + infra validation complete)

I’ll update the MAP file with these entries and label owners for each gate. Marcus, can you add the sample load profile we recommend for the pilot and a short runbook for the remediation loop?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Bloom <emma@aureliushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance tests (Aurelius pilot)

Adding the operational details Emma asked for —

Sample load profile (pilot baseline):
- Concurrent users: 10–15 simulated agents
- Avg requests per minute: 45–60 across the cluster
- Avg request size: ~350 tokens inbound / 60 tokens outbound
- Target 95th pct latency: <150ms for cold path; <80ms for cached responses

Remediation runbook (short):
1) Detect: failing test flagged in test harness -> create ticket in Jira
2) Triage: owner (integration or solutions) reproduces and collects logs + sample payloads
3) Patch: try prompt/config adjustment -> quick retest in staging
4) Escalate: if failure persists, open a severity-2 incident and loop in model ops
5) Re-run: full acceptance suite within 5 business days of fix

I’ve updated MAP-draft.xlsx with owners for these tasks and added a timeline column. Monica — once Emma confirms clinical thresholds we’ll timestamp the go/no-go fixtures and prepare a short SOW addendum that highlights the acceptance-run handoff to procurement.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Manager, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: runbook excerpt (embedded in MAP-draft.xlsx)

From: Aurelius Procurement <procurement@aureliushealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Bloom <emma@aureliushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance tests (Aurelius pilot)

Folks — thanks for looping us in. Two items from procurement:

1) Pricing/SOW: we need a short SOW (1 page) that describes the pilot scope, expected deliverables, and the acceptance gates. We prefer a fixed-fee pilot model. Can Redwood provide draft SOW and final price by EOD Friday (2026-10-09)?
2) Contracting: standard Aurelius terms require a 30-day payment window; we may request a minor confidentiality tweak to allow us to share limited outputs internally. Please note any exceptions in your draft.

If you can provide the SOW and a final MAP with owners/acceptance thresholds, we’ll prioritize internal approvals and aim to issue a PO within the 2–3 week window.

Thanks —
Aaron Patel
